# Herby Chicken Salad on Toast

## Overview
A fresh, herb-loaded chicken salad made with sour cream, whole grain mustard, and lots of fresh dill and parsley, served open-faced on toasted seeded bread and garnished with celery leaves and snap peas.

## Details
- **Servings:** 2-4
- **Prep time:** 15 minutes
- **Cook time:** 0 minutes (using pre-cooked chicken)
- **Total time:** 15 minutes

## Ingredients

### Chicken Salad
- 2 cooked chicken breasts (approx), diced into small cubes
- 3 stalks celery, sliced thin
- 1 handful snap peas/green beans (approx), sliced on a bias
- 1 large bunch fresh dill, finely chopped
- 1 large bunch fresh parsley, finely chopped
- Sour cream, several spoonfuls (approx 1/3–1/2 cup)
- Whole grain mustard, 1-2 spoonfuls (approx)
- 1 lemon — zested and juiced (half the lemon squeezed)
- Salt and pepper, to taste

### For Serving
- Seeded multigrain bread, toasted
- Celery leaves, for garnish
- Sliced snap peas, for garnish

## Instructions

1. **Dice the chicken:** Cut pre-cooked chicken breasts into small, bite-sized cubes on a cutting board. Transfer to a large glass mixing bowl.

2. **Prep the vegetables:** Thinly slice the celery stalks and add to the bowl. Slice the snap peas/green beans on a bias and add to the bowl.

3. **Chop the herbs:** Finely chop a generous amount of fresh dill and parsley together. Add the chopped herbs to the bowl.

4. **Add the dressing ingredients:** Squeeze in the sour cream, add spoonfuls of whole grain mustard, zest the lemon over the bowl using a microplane, then squeeze in the juice from half the lemon.

5. **Season and mix:** Season with salt and pepper, then stir everything together until well combined and creamy.

6. **Toast the bread:** Toast slices of seeded multigrain bread.

7. **Serve:** Pile the chicken salad generously onto the toasted bread. Garnish with celery leaves and thinly sliced snap peas on top. Serve open-faced.

## Chef's Tips
- Use a rotisserie chicken or any leftover cooked chicken for ease
- The snap peas add a nice fresh crunch — taste them raw while prepping to check freshness
- Be generous with the herbs — they make this salad special
- Can also be served on crackers as a snack/appetizer (shown briefly with a cracker)
- The sour cream base makes it lighter than traditional mayo-based chicken salad

## Storage
- Store chicken salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Toast bread fresh when ready to serve.

# Spring Pea & Leek Pasta with Burrata and Toasted Breadcrumbs

## Overview
A vibrant, spring-inspired pasta featuring a silky blended pea and leek sauce with fresh herbs, topped with creamy burrata and crispy toasted breadcrumbs.

## Servings: 2-3 | Prep time: 15 min | Cook time: 20 min | Total time: 35 min

---

## Ingredients

### Pea & Leek Sauce
- 2 large leeks, cleaned and thinly sliced
- 2 cups (approx) green peas (frozen or fresh)
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 bunch fresh dill, chopped
- 1 bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley, chopped
- 1 lemon (zest and juice)
- Olive oil, for sautéing
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Parmesan cheese, finely grated (approx ½ cup)

### Pasta
- 1 lb (454g) Rummo Mezzi Rigatoni No. 51 (or similar short pasta)
- Reserved pasta water

### Toasted Breadcrumbs
- Breadcrumbs (approx ½ cup)
- Olive oil
- Salt and pepper

### Topping
- 1 ball burrata (Lioni Burrata con Panna or similar)
- Extra fresh dill and parsley, for garnish

---

## Instructions

1. **Prep the leeks:** Trim the root end and dark green tops from the leeks. Slice each leek in half lengthwise, then thinly slice into half-moons. Place sliced leeks in a large bowl of cold water and swish around to remove any dirt and grit. Drain and spin dry in a salad spinner.

2. **Prep the herbs and garlic:** Finely chop the fresh dill and Italian parsley. Mince the garlic cloves. Zest the lemon.

3. **Sauté the leeks:** Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the cleaned, sliced leeks and cook, stirring with a wooden spoon, until softened and wilted.

4. **Add aromatics:** Add the chopped dill, parsley, minced garlic, and lemon zest to the softened leeks. Stir to combine and cook for another minute or two until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.

5. **Cook the pasta:** Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the mezzi rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve about 1 cup of pasta water before draining.

6. **Make the pea sauce:** Transfer about half of the leek-herb mixture to a blender. Add the peas and blend until smooth and creamy, adding a splash of pasta water as needed to reach a smooth, saucy consistency.

7. **Combine:** Pour the blended green pea sauce back into the skillet with the remaining sautéed leeks and some reserved whole peas. Add the drained pasta and toss to coat, adding pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese.

8. **Make the toasted breadcrumbs:** In a separate small pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and season with salt and pepper. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Remove from heat.

9. **Serve:** Divide the pasta among bowls. Tear burrata over the top of each serving. Sprinkle generously with toasted breadcrumbs and garnish with extra fresh herbs (dill and parsley).

---

## Chef's Tips
- **Cleaning leeks is essential** — split them lengthwise and soak in water to remove all sand and grit trapped between the layers.
- A **salad spinner** is the easiest way to dry the leeks after washing.
- Save your **pasta water** — the starchy water helps emulsify and thicken the sauce.
- The sauce should be vibrant green; avoid overcooking the peas to maintain the bright color.
- Room temperature burrata is creamier and more luxurious than cold.

## Storage
- Store leftover pasta (without burrata topping) in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water. Add fresh burrata and breadcrumbs when serving.

# Sungold Mascarpone Pasta

## Overview
A luxuriously creamy pasta featuring jammy Sungold tomatoes blended into a silky sauce with mascarpone and Pecorino Romano, topped with crispy bacon. A beautiful way to showcase sweet, peak-season Sungold tomatoes.

- **Servings:** 4
- **Prep time:** 10 minutes
- **Cook time:** 25 minutes
- **Total time:** 35 minutes

---

## Ingredients

### Sauce
- 1 quart Sungold tomatoes
- 4 garlic cloves, roughly chopped
- 4 tablespoons olive oil
- 6 slices bacon, chopped
- 1 cup chicken stock
- 8 oz mascarpone
- Freshly grated Pecorino Romano (plus extra for serving)
- Salt and pepper

### Pasta
- 1 lb pasta (estimated — long noodles such as spaghetti or bucatini work well)
- Reserved pasta water

---

## Instructions

1. **Bring a pot of water to a boil** and heat a large, shallow pan over medium heat.
2. **Roughly chop the garlic** while the pan is heating.
3. **Cook the tomatoes:** Once the pan is hot, add the olive oil and the quart of Sungold tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper, cover, and let them start to get jammy.
4. **Cook the bacon:** In a separate pan, cook the chopped bacon until crispy. Transfer to a paper towel–lined plate and set aside.
5. **Add the garlic** to the tomatoes and cook 2–3 minutes until softened. Pour in the chicken stock, cover, and let the tomatoes and garlic cook about **10 minutes** until soft and jammy.
6. **Blend the sauce** using an immersion blender or a regular blender until smooth. Return to the pan and simmer a bit to thicken.
7. **Stir in the mascarpone** and let it melt completely. Reduce heat to low to keep warm.
8. **Cook the pasta:** Salt the boiling water generously and cook the pasta **2 minutes less** than the package instructions (for finishing in the sauce).
9. **Combine:** Use tongs to transfer the pasta directly to the sauce, letting pasta water cling to the noodles. Stir in freshly grated Pecorino Romano. If the sauce is too thick or not glossy enough, add a splash of pasta water. Taste for salt after adding pasta water.
10. **Plate and garnish** with crispy bacon, extra Pecorino Romano, and freshly cracked pepper.

---

## Chef's Tips

- **Make-ahead sauce:** You can make the sauce ahead and keep it in the fridge for a couple of days. Make it up until the point of adding the mascarpone, then squeeze in a little lemon juice before storing.
- **Freezing Sungold tomatoes:** Sungold tomato season is short — if you want to make this pasta later, you can freeze your Sungold tomatoes and use them in place of fresh.
- **Pasta water is key:** Transferring the pasta with tongs (rather than draining) lets starchy pasta water cling to the noodles, which helps emulsify and loosen the sauce.

---

## Storage

Store leftover sauce (without mascarpone) in the fridge for up to 2–3 days with a squeeze of lemon juice. Sungold tomatoes can be frozen for future use in this recipe.

# Seafood Fregola

## Overview
A flavorful Mediterranean-inspired dish featuring fregola (Sardinian pearl-shaped pasta) cooked with a mix of seafood, creating a rich and hearty one-pot meal.

> **Note:** This recipe is based on a short 1-minute TikTok video with limited detail. Several measurements and steps are estimated based on standard preparations of this classic dish.

---

**Servings:** 2–3 (estimated)
**Prep time:** 15 minutes (estimated)
**Cook time:** 25 minutes (estimated)
**Total time:** 40 minutes (estimated)

---

## Ingredients

- 250g fregola sarda (Sardinian couscous/pasta)
- 200g clams, scrubbed and cleaned
- 200g mussels, scrubbed and debearded
- 150g prawns/shrimp, shell-on or peeled (estimated)
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 3–4 cloves garlic, sliced
- 1 small shallot or onion, finely diced (estimated)
- 150ml white wine (estimated)
- 400g cherry tomatoes, halved (or canned crushed tomatoes)
- 500ml fish or seafood stock (estimated)
- 1 teaspoon chili flakes (to taste)
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
- Lemon wedges, for serving

---

## Instructions

1. **Toast the fregola:** In a large pan or skillet, toast the fregola in a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat until lightly golden and fragrant, about 2–3 minutes. Set aside.

2. **Build the base:** In the same pan, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Sauté the garlic and shallot until softened and fragrant, about 1–2 minutes. Add chili flakes.

3. **Add tomatoes:** Add the cherry tomatoes and cook until they begin to break down, about 3–4 minutes.

4. **Deglaze:** Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half, about 2 minutes.

5. **Cook the fregola:** Add the toasted fregola and fish stock. Stir to combine, bring to a simmer, and cook for about 10–12 minutes until the fregola is nearly al dente and has absorbed most of the liquid.

6. **Add the seafood:** Nestle the clams and mussels into the pan first (they take longer), followed by the prawns. Cover and cook for 4–5 minutes until the shells open and the prawns are pink and cooked through. Discard any shellfish that don't open.

7. **Finish and serve:** Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

---

## Chef's Tips

- **Fregola substitute:** If you can't find fregola, Israeli/pearl couscous makes a good substitute.
- **Toasting is key:** Don't skip toasting the fregola — it adds a nutty depth of flavor.
- **Seafood variations:** You can add calamari, scallops, or any firm white fish.
- **Liquid adjustment:** Add more stock as needed — fregola absorbs a lot of liquid. The final dish should be slightly brothy, not dry.

---

## Storage

- Best enjoyed fresh. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to **1 day**. Reheat gently with a splash of stock. Note that shellfish does not reheat well, so this dish is ideally made to order.
